newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian court jails two for tourist attacks plot.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian court jails two for tourist attacks plot.

text.p: Jordan's state security court on Tuesday sentenced two Jordanians to lengthy prison terms for plotting attacks against tourists, judicial sources said.

Salem al-Jaradat, 22, was sentenced to death, commuted to life imprisonment with hard labour on three charges of possession and manufacture of firearms and plotting "to wage terrorist attacks against tourists". Ahmad al-Soub, 22, was jailed for 10 years for "planning terrorist actions."
Both belong to prominent Jordanian tribes.

They had been charged with involvement in an attack on a French diplomat, who was wounded in a shootout in February last year about 100 km (60 miles) south of Amman. A criminal court squashed those charges earlier this year.
Both men are believed opposed to a tourism industry that has attracted rising numbers of Israelis to Jordan.
According to earlier court documents, the two wanted to hijack a tourist bus that visits the desolate hilly Mujeb area and blow it up to harm the tourism industry.
